key_facts: lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes are unaffected
some lesions have resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
skin biopsy shows nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis shows hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils

raw.rationale: The presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene on RT-PCR in the bone marrow analysis is a specific diagnostic marker for this condition, which also explains the patient's hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase level, and skin lesions.

rejected.label: Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia
rejected.why: While the patient has features of chronic eosinophilic leukemia, the specific FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene is diagnostic for FIP1L1-PDGFRA-Associated Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia, making this a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hypereosinophilic Syndrome
rejected.why: Hypereosinophilic syndrome is a broader category that encompasses various conditions with hypereosinophilia. The presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene and other specific findings in this case point towards a more specific diagnosis of FIP1L1-PDGFRA-Associated Chronic Eosinophilic Leukemia.
